pr.integration: Already merged before this session. This reconciliation is not a new merge and must not be counted twice.

acceptance.summary: KernelSnapshot::save now uses the shared durable publication primitive rather than truncating the destination. Private exclusive temporary creation, pre-rename file sync, Unix directory/ancestor sync and explicit failure semantics are integrated and tested.
verified_properties: JSON snapshot format and bounded no-follow loads remain unchanged.
Temporary sibling uses create_new and Unix mode(0600) at open, before writing contents.
File contents and metadata are synchronized before rename; Unix parent and ancestor directory sync failures propagate.
An injected partial write preserves the old complete target and cleans the temporary file; retry succeeds.
An injected directory-sync failure after publication returns an error without claiming rollback or confirmed durability.
Snapshots replace existing files with a new private inode; interrupted-attempt debris and non-regular outputs are covered.
limitations: Fault injection and stale temporary files are not hardware power-cut qualification.
The parent namespace must be trusted; this primitive is neither a path sandbox nor a replacement CAS.
Directory sync remains best-effort outside Unix; no universal power-loss durability is claimed.
CCOS-Enterprise's vendored copy was not synchronized by this PR; MEM-08 remains open.

coverage: debug and release tests, doctests, Rust 1.89 MSRV
format, strict Clippy, feature build matrix, author/hygiene checks
cognitive tests, replay equivalence, snapshot differential/roundtrip and schema compatibility
documentation build, dependency/license/SBOM checks, secret detection
strict BEIR parser/CLI and genuinely enabled LLM harness tests
